newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends sharply up on relief over rates.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends sharply up on relief over rates.

text.p: Key March Euroyen futures closed the Tuesday session higher on the Tokyo International Financial Futures Exchange (TIFFE), relieved by expectations Japan's easy credit stance will be maintained for the time being, traders said.
The expectations were sparked by a government official's comment, following the announcement of gross domestic product (GDP) data on Friday, they said.
"We expect that we won't have a credit-tightening at least until the end of this year," said a trader at a Japanese financial institution.

Traders said Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Vice Minister Shinpei Nukaya's comment on Friday that the government did not need to consider additional government spending to prop up the economy, despite a drop in the April-June GDP, prompted them to believe the Bank of Japan will not be able to tighten its credit stance for a while.
GDP fell a real 0.7 percent in the April to June period from the previous quarter, official data showed on Friday.

Moderate U.S. growth and benign inflation proved by the recent U.S. economic data raised hopes that the Fed will not raise interest rates at its next policy meeting on September 24 and helped to soothe Japan's rate jitters, traders said.
But they said little scope was expected to be left on the upside of the key March futures.
"It doesn't mean that the BOJ will guide the interest rates lower or cut its discount rate. So I don't expect the futures to gain much from this level," he said.
On the money market, the BOJ conducted a neutral operation on the first day of the current reserve reporting period.
This morning, the BOJ drained 500 billion yen from the market, in the face of a net fund surplus of 500 billion yen.
The key overnight unsecured call rate was mostly traded at 0.47 percent on Tuesday. Friday's weighted average was 0.46 percent.
The market was closed on Monday for a national holiday.
In the long end of the market, the key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued at 0.53 percent on Tuesday, unchanged since September 3. Volume was estimated at 60 billion yen.
